answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and registers one bridge route. A violet seal binds its key to its bridge segment and spiral order, so checks follow spiral sequence. Auditors recount the ledger; a skipped segment, reused seal, or out-of-order spiral check burns the bond. First registration costs 30 credits, the kth pays 30+6(k-1), the 1000th pays 6024, and 1000 fakes pay 3,027,000 plus 70,000 locked. An honest agent pays 30 once and recovers its bond. A rented-lane ring fails: a rented violet seal mismatches the renter key on its bridge segment, burning both bonds.
